## Abstract IJDS candidato

We study credit portfolio selection when calibrated default probabilities remain
too uncertain to support point-estimate optimization alone. We propose Conformal
Robust Predict-then-Optimize (CRPTO), a post-hoc and auditable framework that
maps Mondrian conformal prediction intervals into robust portfolio constraints.
On a 276,869-loan out-of-time Lending Club evaluation, the promoted economic
policy earns USD 170.5K on a USD 1M budget while passing the exact alpha=0.01
funded-set bound, with weighted miscoverage V=0.03645, conformal premium
Gamma_CP=0.18591, and zero robust-constraint violation. The full promoted robust
region contains 45/45 alpha01-safe policies, which reduces the risk that the
result is a single-point artifact. The contribution is not a higher AUC
leaderboard result, but a reproducible bridge from calibrated probabilistic
learning to auditable robust credit decisions. The framework clarifies the trade
off between return, conformal coverage, and governance: decision-focused
learning can reduce regret, while CRPTO provides coverage-aware constraints,
traceable funded-set composition, and model-risk-management evidence suitable
for regulated credit settings.
